A ratio that indicates liquidity. Higher ratios suggest the asset is more actively traded and easier to buy/sell near its true value. Lower ratios may mean less liquidity and greater price volatility. The portion of total supply that is publicly available and actively circulating in the market. The number of tokens that currently exist, minus any coins that have been burned. This is similar to “shares outstanding” in equities. The maximum number of coins that could ever exist, based on the project’s code or rules. For some cryptocurrencies, this is a fixed number (e.g., Bitcoin’s 21M cap).
